summary: Robert P. Scharlemann worked in religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Concordia College, Concordia Seminary, and Heidelberg University, later holding posts at the University of Southern California (~1966–1968), University of Iowa (~1968–1981), and University of Virginia (~1981–2004).
Robert P. Weller is a scholar of sinology and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Johns Hopkins University (1975–1981) and became a professor at Boston University in 1990.

Robert Paget Dewhurst was a scholar in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He completed an M.A. at the University of Oxford in 1888 and served there as University Lecturer in Hindustani in 1924.

Robert Ripley Moore was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Bethel College (~1952–1956) and the University of Michigan (~1960–1965), taught at Mussoorie College, and was Assistant Professor of Indo-Aryan Linguistics at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1965–1966).

Robert S. Ellwood specialized in religious studies and Japanology. He studied at the University of Colorado, Yale University, and under Mircea Eliade at the University of Chicago (~1964–1967), before holding a post at the University of Southern California (~1967–1997).

Robert S. Nelson is an art historian and archaeologist who studied at Rice University (~1965–1969) and New York University (~1970–1978). He served as a professor at the University of Chicago (~1974–2005) and joined Yale University around 2005.

Robert S. P. Beekes worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at Leiden University (~1956–1969) under F. B. J. Kuiper. He held posts at the Marnix Gymnasium and later at Leiden University in 1973 and 1979.

Robert Schram worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He earned his PhD and PD at the University of Vienna (1869–1874), worked at Geneva Observatory, Militärgeographisches Institut, and was affiliated with the University of Vienna.

Robert Sewell worked in Indology, history, and archaeology after studying at Radley College (~1858–1863). He served in the Indian Civil Service (~1868–1894), as Keeper at Tamil Nadu Archives, and as a Fellow of the University of Madras.
Robert Seymour Conway was a linguist who studied at the City of London School (~1876–1883). He held posts at Newnham College, Cambridge (~1887–1893) and Gonville and Caius College (~1888–1894).

Robert Tegethoff works in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Indology. He earned an M.A. at the University of Cologne (2015–2018) and holds positions as a researcher and postdoc at the Free University of Berlin (attested 2026).
Robert Vane Russell specialized in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Trinity College, Cambridge (~1892–1895) and served in the Indian Civil Service from ~1895 to 1915.
Robert Warren Clark is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under doctoral supervisor Karen Christina Lang and adviser K. L. Seshagiri Rao (attested 1994).

Robert Watson Frazer was an Indologist who studied at Rathmines School and Trinity College Dublin under Robert Atkinson. He served in the Indian Civil Service (~1877–1886) and lectured in Telugu and Tamil at UCL (1885–1916) and SOAS (1917–1919).
Robert Wilson Ievers was an Indologist, historian, and archaeologist who earned an M.A. at Queen's University Belfast. In 1872, he entered the Ceylon Civil Service as a civil servant.

Robert Xavier Murphy worked in Indology, linguistics, and history and archaeology. He served as a master at the Bombay Native Education Society and as secretary of the Bombay Chamber of Commerce and Industry in 1839.

Robert Zimmermann was an Indologist and scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at St Beuno's and Humboldt University of Berlin under Heinrich Lüders, later serving as professor at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai (1914–1930).

Robert Zydenbos works in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at Utrecht University (~1975–1989) and held posts at the University of Toronto (~1999–2001) and the University of Munich (~2001).

Robert van Gulik was a scholar of sinology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Leiden University and Utrecht University under C. C. Uhlenbeck, J. J. L. Duyvendak, and Jan Gonda, later becoming a professor at Utrecht in 1967.

Robert von Heine-Geldern worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Munich and Vienna under Wilhelm Schmidt, and held posts at the University of Vienna, Columbia University (1938–1941), and the Asia Institute (1943–1949).
